subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Insurance Fraud
description: A micro-lesson that makes Insurance Fraud usable.

hook.text: A man fakes his own death so his wife can collect the insurance. He's found alive three years later.

buildup.text: Insurance fraud costs over $80 billion per year in the US. It ranges from staged accidents to fake claims.

discovery.text: Soft fraud — exaggerating legitimate claims — is far more common than hard fraud like staged events.

twist.text: Fraud raises premiums for everyone. Honest policyholders pay an extra $400-700 per year because of it.

climax.text: Insurance companies invest heavily in fraud detection, but the sheer volume of claims makes it overwhelming.

punchline.text: $80 billion a year. You pay for other people's fraud.

quiz.question: How much does insurance fraud cost in the US annually?
